disable-publishing.description: If yes, runs avahi-daemon in querying-only mode without publishing any records.

disable-user-service-publishing.description: If yes, prevents user applications from publishing services while keeping address records.

disallow-other-stacks.description: If yes, prevents other processes from binding to UDP port 5353 to secure mDNS traffic.

domain-name.description: Set the default domain name avahi-daemon registers its host name and services on.

enable-dbus.description: Controls D-Bus connection; 'warn' starts up even on connection failure and attempts reconnection.

enable-reflector.description: If yes, reflects incoming mDNS requests to all local network interfaces.

enable-wide-area.description: Enable wide-area DNS-SD, allowing resolution of non-.local domains via unicast DNS.

entries-per-entry-group-max.description: Maximum number of resource records per entry group registered by a D-Bus client.

host-name.description: Set the host name avahi-daemon tries to register on the LAN.

host-name-from-machine-id.description: If set to yes, avahi-daemon will use the machine-id as the LAN name.

objects-per-client-max.description: Maximum number of objects registered per D-Bus client at a time.

publish-a-on-ipv6.description: If yes, publishes IPv4 A records via IPv6 transport.

publish-aaaa-on-ipv4.description: If yes, publishes IPv6 AAAA records via IPv4 transport.

publish-addresses.description: If yes, registers mDNS address records for all local IP addresses.

publish-dns-servers.description: Set a comma separated list of IP addresses for unicast DNS servers to announce via mDNS.

publish-domain.description: If yes, announces the locally used domain name for browsing by other hosts.

publish-hinfo.description: If yes, registers an mDNS HINFO record containing local OS and CPU information.

publish-resolv-conf-dns-servers.description: If yes, publishes unicast DNS servers specified in /etc/resolv.conf.

publish-workstation.description: If yes, registers a _workstation._tcp service for administrative LAN browsing.

ratelimit-interval-usec.description: Per-interface packet rate-limiting interval parameter in microseconds.

reflect-filters.description: Set a comma separated list of allowed service names to be reflected to other networks.

reflect-ipv.description: If yes, forwards mDNS traffic between IPv4 and IPv6 when reflector is enabled.

rlimit-as.description: Maximum size of the process's virtual memory in bytes.

rlimit-core.description: Maximum core file size in bytes.

rlimit-data.description: Maximum size of the process's data segment in bytes.

rlimit-fsize.description: Maximum size of files the process may create in bytes.

rlimit-nofile.description: Maximum number of open file descriptors.

rlimit-nproc.description: Maximum number of processes a user can launch.

rlimit-stack.description: Maximum size of the process stack in bytes.

use-iff-running.description: If yes, monitors IFF_RUNNING flag to automatically announce services on connected networks.

use-ipv4.description: If no, avahi-daemon will not use IPv4 sockets.

use-ipv6.description: If no, avahi-daemon will not use IPv6 sockets.

language.description: Language code for reports (e.g., 'en', 'fr', 'de', 'ja'). Must match one of the languages installed with AWStats.

site_domain.description: Primary domain name for this AWStats configuration. Only log entries matching this domain (or aliases) will be processed.

timezone.description: Timezone offset in hours from UTC (e.g., -5 for EST, +1 for CET). Used to align reports with local time. Matches the timezone plugin parameter LoadPlugin="timezone +{{ timezone }}".

AllowMail.description: Which users are allowed to use axmail (all, nologin, passwd, axhome)

AutoCreate.description: Allow automatic creation of user accounts (yes/no)

AutoGroup.description: Group name or ID for auto-created accounts

FaxGate.description: Fax gateway email address (must be quoted in config)

First_uid.description: First user ID to use for auto-created accounts

HomeDir.description: Base directory for home directories of new users

IdleTimeout.description: Idle timeout in seconds before disconnecting inactive connections

Last_uid.description: Maximum user ID to use for auto-created accounts

SysopMail.description: Sysop's email address for mail handling

archive_prefix.description: Prefix for backup filenames (used as VOLNAME); e.g., 'myhost-backup' → 'myhost-backup-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz'

backup_dir.description: Absolute path to the directory where backup archives will be stored

max_full_backups.description: Maximum number of full backups to retain; older full backups will be deleted

emailto.description: Email address (local part only) to receive backup reports.

masterlogfile.description: Where the main backupninja log file is located.

reporthost.description: Remote host to rsync backupninja logs for aggregation. Empty string means disabled.

reportinfo.description: Include info messages from handlers in email reports.

reportprom.description: Produce prometheus metrics of backup status.

reportspace.description: Include disk space usage in backup email reports.

reportsuccess.description: Send email report even if all modules succeeded.

reportwarning.description: Send email report even if there were no errors.

tmpdir.description: Directory where all the backup configuration files live.

barman_home.description: Root directory where Barman stores its configuration, logs, and backup metadata.

barman_locks.description: Directory for Barman lock files (used for concurrent operation safety).

barman_log_file.description: Path to the main Barman log file.

parallel_jobs.description: Maximum number of parallel jobs for backup and recovery operations.

servers_conf_dir.description: Subdirectory of /etc/barman.d/ where server configuration files are placed (default: empty string for /etc/barman.d/, or e.g. 'conf.d' for /etc/barman.d/conf.d/).

admin.description: XMPP JID (bare or full) of the service administrator. Receives operational notices and errors.

hostname.description: The hostname this XMPP-to-IRC gateway will advertise to XMPP clients.

port.description: The port on which the XMPP component listens for incoming connections (typically 5347 for XMPP components).

realname_customization.description: Allow per-user customization of the realname sent to IRC servers.

realname_from_jid.description: Use the JID (instead of hostname) to generate the realname if realname_customization=true.

xmpp_server_ip.description: IP address of the XMPP server to which biboumi connects.

defaultscheme.description: Protocol scheme assumed when missing from a URL (gopher/gemini/http/https)

args.description: Arguments to pass to the command as positional parameters ($1...$9,$*,$@).

uservars.description: Number of user variables ($BOSHVAR1, $BOSHVAR2, …) to allocate.

replyto.description: Status ID to link replies to.

user.description: Target username for 'user' or 'direct' actions.

show_table_scroll_position.description: Show scroll position tracker in table widget titles

time_delta.description: Time change per zoom step (ms); minimum 1000 ms

MaxJobs.description: Sets the maximum number of concurrent jobs allowed.

MaxJobsPerPrinter.description: Sets the maximum number of concurrent jobs allowed per printer.

MaxJobsPerUser.description: Sets the maximum number of concurrent jobs allowed per user.

MaxLogSize.description: Sets the maximum size of log files in bytes before rotation.

MaxSubscriptions.description: Sets the maximum number of concurrent event subscriptions allowed.

MaxSubscriptionsPerJob.description: Sets the maximum number of concurrent subscriptions allowed per job.

MaxSubscriptionsPerPrinter.description: Sets the maximum number of concurrent subscriptions allowed per printer.

MaxSubscriptionsPerUser.description: Sets the maximum number of concurrent subscriptions allowed per user.

MultipleOperationTimeout.description: Sets the maximum allowed time in seconds between files in a multi-file job.

Order.description: Controls whether Allow or Deny directives are evaluated first.

Port.description: Waits for connections on the specified port number.

PreserveJobFiles.description: Sets whether job files are retained after printing.

PreserveJobHistory.description: Sets whether job history is retained after printing.

ReadyPaperSizes.description: Sets a list of paper sizes to report as ready/loaded.

ReloadTimeout.description: Sets the time in seconds to wait for jobs to finish before restarting the scheduler.

Require.description: Specifies required users, groups, or valid-user for access.

SSLListen.description: Waits for encrypted connections on the specified address and port.

SSLOptions.description: Sets encryption/TLS protocol and algorithm options.

SSLPort.description: Waits for encrypted connections on the specified port.

Satisfy.description: Sets whether all or any access/authentication conditions must be met.

ServerAdmin.description: Sets the email address of the server administrator.

ServerAlias.description: Sets alternative hostnames for HTTP Host header validation.

ServerName.description: Sets the fully qualified hostname of the server.

ServerTokens.description: Sets what information is included in the Server header of HTTP responses.

StrictConformance.description: Sets whether the scheduler requires clients to strictly follow IPP specifications.

SubscriptionPrivateAccess.description: Sets an access list for private subscription values.

SubscriptionPrivateValues.description: Sets the list of subscription values that should be private.

Timeout.description: Sets the HTTP timeout in seconds.

WebInterface.description: Sets whether the web interface is enabled.

Plugin.acc.X.description: Maps the accelerometer X axis to a standard input event.

Plugin.acc.Y.description: Maps the accelerometer Y axis to a standard input event.

Plugin.led.Battery.description: Enables the battery check function when set to 1.

Plugin.led.Button.description: Sets the button combination to trigger the battery check function.

include.description: Includes an external configuration file or directive block.

auth_strategy.description: Authentication strategy; commonly 'keystone' for OpenStack deployments.

debug.description: Enable debug mode for detailed logging.

log_dir.description: Directory where Cyborg log files are stored.

log_file.description: Path to the log file for the Cyborg service.

use_syslog.description: Whether to send log output to syslog.

verbose.description: Enable verbose output for debugging and troubleshooting.

binary_check.description: Whether to perform binary format checks

color_ui.description: Whether to enable colored UI output

module_load_all.description: Whether to load all modules automatically

acceptable.description: Minimum acceptable client duration in seconds.

attempts.description: Number of respawn attempts before delaying.

bind.description: Terminate client when user logs out (Linux/systemd-elogind only).

chdir.description: Change the current directory before running the client.

command.description: Specify the client command and its arguments.

core.description: Allow the client to create a core file.

delay.description: Delay in seconds between respawn attempt bursts.

env.description: Set an environment variable for the client process.

errlog.description: Destination for daemon's error output (syslog spec or file path).

foreground.description: Run the client in the foreground.

limit.description: Maximum number of respawn attempt bursts.

pidfile.description: Override pidfile name and location.

pty.description: Allocate a pseudo terminal for the client.

read-eof.description: Read client output until EOF after SIGCHLD.

respawn.description: Respawn the client when it terminates.

safe.description: Disallow reading unsafe config files or executing unsafe binaries.

umask.description: Set the file creation umask (must be valid octal).

unsafe.description: Allow reading unsafe config files or executing unsafe binaries.

DAPTUP_CHECK_FOR_OUTDATED_PACKAGES.description: Enable check for outdated packages (preparing long ago, with newer candidates available). Possible values: "n" (no), "y" (yes). (reused from existing: y|n enum)

DAPTUP_DISABLE_COLUMNS.description: Disable column output (pass --disable-columns to aptitude). Possible values: "n" (no), "y" (yes). Only effective with newer aptitude versions. (reused from existing: y|n enum)

DAPTUP_HOOK_ENABLED.description: Whether Daptup gathers and shows information on each 'apt-get/aptitude/cupt update' invocation. Possible values: "n" (no), "y" (yes). (reused from existing: y|n enum)

DAPTUP_MINIMAL_DAY_COUNT_TREATING_OUTDAT.description: Minimum age (in days) for a package to be treated as 'outdated'. (reused from existing)

DAPTUP_NEW_DISPLAY_FORMAT.description: Format string passed to aptitude for new packages changes output. See aptitude docs. (reused from existing)

DAPTUP_NEW_DISPLAY_WIDTH.description: Maximum line width for aptitude output of new package changes (requires aptitude). (reused from existing)

DAPTUP_NEW_INCLUDE_DESCRIPTION.description: Include short descriptions when building list of available packages. Possible values: "n" (no), "y" (yes). (reused from existing: y|n enum)

DAPTUP_PACKAGES_WATCH_FOR.description: Space-separated list of package names or regex patterns to watch (even if not installed). Regexes may not use ^ or $. (reused from existing)

DAPTUP_SHOW_CHANGES_IN_POST.description: Whether to show changes after updating the lists (in --post call). Possible values: "n" (no), "y" (yes). (reused from existing: y|n enum)

DAPTUP_USE_COLOR.description: Use colored output. Possible values: "n" (no), "y" (yes). (reused from existing: y|n enum)

DAPTUP_WATCH_DISPLAY_FORMAT.description: Format string passed to aptitude for watched packages changes output. See aptitude docs. (reused from existing)

DAPTUP_WATCH_DISPLAY_WIDTH.description: Maximum line width for aptitude output of watched package changes (requires aptitude). (reused from existing)

dav_ca_cert_file.description: Path to a custom CA certificate bundle file (PEM format). If empty, system defaults are used.

dav_cache_dir.description: Local directory for file content caching. Set to '' (empty string) to disable caching entirely (read-only fallback only).

dav_cache_group.description: Group (name or GID) to own cache files and directories.

dav_cache_owner.description: User (name or UID) to own cache files and directories. Must have read/write access to cache_dir.

dav_cache_size_kb.description: Minimum free space (KB) to maintain on the cache directory. When free space drops below this, davfs2 will purge old cached content.

dav_cache_timeout.description: Time in seconds before cached metadata is considered stale. Lower values reduce consistency but improve freshness.

dav_cert_verification.description: Whether to verify WebDAV server certificates over HTTPS. Disable only for testing or with self-signed certs (not recommended in production).

dav_client_cert.description: Path to a client certificate (PEM format). Required only if the server requires mutual TLS authentication.

dav_client_key.description: Path to the private key for the client certificate. Required if client_cert is set.

dav_compression.description: Enable HTTP compression (gzip) for uploads. May improve performance over slow links but can increase CPU usage.

dav_debug.description: Enable debug logging (requires restart to take effect).

dav_dir_mode.description: Octal permissions for newly created directories (e.g., '0755', '0700').

dav_file_mode.description: Octal file permissions for newly created files (e.g., '0644', '0600').

dav_keep_alive.description: Use HTTP/1.1 persistent connections to reduce handshake overhead. Generally safe to enable.

dav_max_conns.description: Maximum number of concurrent connections per WebDAV server. Increase for better throughput on high-latency links.

dav_proxy.description: Proxy server in 'host:port' format (e.g., 'proxy.example.com:3128'). Leave blank to connect directly.

dav_use_locks.description: Enable WebDAV file locking. Disable if the server does not support locking or causes hangs.

dav_use_mmap.description: Use memory-mapped I/O for cached files (improves performance). Disable only if compatibility issues arise.

config_diagnostics.description: Enable diagnostic output; set to 1 to make config errors fatal, 0 to ignore them.

min_proto_dtls.description: Minimum DTLS protocol version (e.g., '1.2') for system_default.

min_proto_tls.description: Minimum TLS protocol version (e.g., '1.2') for system_default.

oid_section.description: Name of section containing custom OIDs (e.g., 'oids').

openssl_conf.description: Name of the initialization section containing module selectors.

rng_properties.description: Property query string for RNG and underlying algorithms.

rng_seed_properties.description: Property query for the randomness source.

rng_type.description: Random bit generator type: CTR-DRBG, HASH-DRBG, or HMAC-DRBG.

davmail_allow_untrusted_certificates.description: Allow connections to Exchange servers using self-signed or untrusted certificates (security risk).

davmail_authentication.description: Authentication method: 'basic' (HTTP Basic Auth) or 'ntlm' (NTLMv2 for Windows domain).

davmail_connectionTimeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds before giving up on establishing a connection to Exchange.

davmail_host.description: Hostname or IP address of your Exchange server.

davmail_imapIdle.description: Enable IMAP IDLE support for real-time push notifications (requires client support).

davmail_imapPort.description: Port for IMAP service (default: 1143). Set to 0 to disable IMAP.

davmail_keyPassword.description: Password for the private key inside the keystore (if different from keystore password).

davmail_keystore.description: Path to Java keystore file containing the server certificate and private key.

davmail_listen.description: Enable or disable the DavMail server. Set to 'false' to stop the server without uninstalling.

davmail_logFile.description: Full path to the log file.

davmail_maxConnections.description: Maximum number of simultaneous connections to Exchange.

davmail_ntlmDomain.description: Windows domain name, required when using NTLM authentication.

davmail_ntlmHost.description: Host (NetBIOS) name of the client workstation, required by some NTLM setups.

davmail_path_exchange.description: URL path to the Exchange web service endpoint (varies by Exchange version).

davmail_popDeletePolicy.description: When to delete messages from Exchange after POP retrieval: 'never', 'onRead', 'onTrash', or 'afterDays:N'.

davmail_popMaxMessages.description: Maximum number of messages per POP session.

davmail_popPort.description: Port for POP3 service (default: 1110). Set to 0 to disable POP3.

davmail_port.description: IMAP default port (used if no specific IMAP port is configured).

davmail_port_exchange.description: Port on which Exchange listens for the selected protocol (usually 443 for HTTPS).

davmail_protocol.description: Protocol to use for connecting to Exchange: 'auto', 'owa', 'ews', or 'exchange2007_sp1_ews'.

davmail_proxy_host.description: Optional HTTP proxy host (e.g., for outbound connections in corporate networks).

davmail_serverId.description: Unique identifier for the DavMail server (used by Outlook to distinguish multiple gateways).

davmail_smtpAllowLocalFrom.description: Allow 'From:' headers to use local-domain addresses (e.g., @localhost).

davmail_smtpAuth.description: Require authentication for sending mail via SMTP (recommended).

davmail_smtpPort.description: Port for SMTP service (default: 1025). Set to 0 to disable SMTP.

davmail_smtpRequireAuth.description: If true, reject unauthenticated SMTP attempts (even if smtpAuth=false).

davmail_smtpStarttls.description: Enable STARTTLS for SMTP (upgrade to TLS after connection).

davmail_smtpUseSSL.description: Enable SSL for SMTP (connect over SSL from the start).

davmail_socketTimeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds for socket read operations.

davmail_ssl.description: Enable SSL/TLS encryption for the main port. Requires keystore configuration.

davmail_truststore.description: Path to Java truststore containing trusted CA certificates (for validating Exchange server certificate).

davmail_username.description: Exchange username (if not using per-user credentials in mailboxes section).

davmail_webPort.description: Port for the web UI (used only if web_enabled=true).

davmail_web_enabled.description: Enable built-in web UI for diagnostics and status (port 8080 by default).

nvdimm_uuid.description: UUID of the NVDIMM device to reconfigure

subsection_name.description: Unique identifier for the reconfigure-device subsection; must be unique across all config files

sysconfdir.description: Base directory for system configuration files

beacon_addr.description: ASM beacon group address (with optional port, e.g., '224.0.1.1:10001' or 'ff02::1:10001').

bootstrap_addr.description: Bootstrap peer address to use when ASM is broken but SSM works.

dump_file.description: Path to periodic dump file in XML format.

interface.description: Network interface to use for multicast (e.g., 'eth0').

ipv4_only.description: Force IPv4 usage (overrides default IPv6 preference).

local_addr.description: Local source address for multicast packets (e.g., '192.0.2.1').

name.description: The name identifying this beacon instance (defaults to hostname if omitted).

pidfile.description: Path to PID file for daemonized instance.

program_to_launch.description: Program to run after each dump. First argument will be dump filename.

ssm_group.description: SSM group address (with optional port, e.g., '232.1.2.3:10001').

ssm_send.description: Enable SSM data sending in addition to ASM (i.e., -O).

verbose.description: Verbosity level; value determines number of -v flags.

auth_method.description: Authentication method for clients (none = open, password = basic auth, cert = mutual TLS).

cache_size_mb.description: Size of the in-memory query result cache in megabytes.

db_path.description: Absolute path to the directory where database files (indices, data, cache) are stored.

enable_compression.description: Whether to compress stored records to save disk space and I/O (may increase CPU usage).

idle_timeout_sec.description: Maximum idle time (in seconds) before a client connection is closed.

listen_address.description: IP address the service listens on (e.g., 127.0.0.1 for localhost only, or 0.0.0.0 for all interfaces).

listen_port.description: TCP port number for client connections.

log_file.description: Path to the log file. Use 'stdout' to log directly to the console.

log_level.description: Verbosity level for logging (debug, info, warn, error).

max_connections.description: Maximum number of concurrent client connections allowed.

password_file.description: Path to the file containing usernames and hashed passwords (used when auth_method = password).

query_timeout_sec.description: Maximum allowed time (in seconds) for a single query before it is aborted.

tls_cert.description: Path to the server TLS certificate (PEM format), required when auth_method = cert.

tls_key.description: Path to the server TLS private key (PEM format), required when auth_method = cert.

worker_threads.description: Number of worker threads for parallel query processing. Set to match available CPU cores.

allow_anonymous.description: If true, allow ANONYMOUS auth mechanism (insecure unless explicitly designed)

fork.description: If true, fork into background (equivalent to <fork/>)

include_dir_ignore_missing.description: If true, missing files in include_dir are ignored

keep_umask.description: If true, retain original umask after forking

pidfile.description: Path to write PID file

policies[].at_console.description: If true, applies to console sessions; if false, to non-console

run_as_user.description: Username or UID to run daemon as (e.g., messagebus, root, _example)

selinux_associations[].context.description: SELinux target context for acquiring the name (e.g., 'foo_t')

selinux_enabled.description: If true, enable SELinux configuration (must have <selinux> block)

servicehelper.description: SetUID helper to launch system services (e.g., /usr/lib/dbus-1.0/dbus-daemon-launch-helper)

standard_session_servicedirs.description: If true, use standard session service directories (session bus only)

standard_system_servicedirs.description: If true, use standard system service directories (system bus only)

syslog.description: If true, log to syslog (command-line overrides)

chroot.description: If true, chroot into LibDir before running services — only use if security hardening is required and services support it.

dbus_bus.description: D-Bus bus type: 'system' or 'session'. Set by the package and rarely changed.

dbus_name.description: D-Bus service name used by oddjobd.

dbus_path.description: D-Bus object path implemented by oddjobd.

debug.description: Enable verbose debug logging to the system log (syslog/journald). Turn on only for troubleshooting.

group.description: System group under which the daemon runs.

lib_dir.description: Path to the directory containing oddjob helper programs. Usually set by the package installer.

max_threads.description: Maximum number of worker threads. Set to 0 for no limit (but system resources still apply).

pid_file.description: Full path to the file where the daemon writes its process ID.

run_dir.description: Directory for transient runtime files used by the daemon and its helpers.

session_tracking.description: Enable PAM session tracking. Required for services that need to interact with user sessions (e.g., mounting user home directories).

user.description: System user under which the oddjobd daemon process runs. Should have minimal privileges.

context.description: Sets the policy scope to apply to all users by default.

own.description: D-Bus bus name allowed or denied for ownership.

send_destination.description: D-Bus destination bus name allowed or denied for sending messages.

send_interface.description: D-Bus interface name allowed or denied for sending messages.

user.description: Restricts subsequent policy rules to a specific system user.

allow-root.description: Allow daemon to run as root. If this option is not provided the daemon will refuse to run as the root user.

dbus-name.description: Claim the given name on dbus.

flush-all.description: Flush all objects and sessions when daemon is started.

logger.description: Direct logging output to named logging target.

prng-seed-file.description: Read seed for pseudo-random number generator from the provided file.

session.description: Connect daemon to the session dbus instead of the system dbus.

tcti.description: Provide the daemon with a string that describes the TCTI and how to configure it for communication with the next component down the TSS2 stack.

system-db.description: Specifies the system-level dconf database to load for IBus configuration.

user-db.description: Specifies the user-level dconf database to load for IBus configuration.

leases.backend.description: Lease storage backend. 'file' persists leases across restarts; 'memory' resets on reload.

leases.path.description: Path to the lease file when using the 'file' backend. Ignored for 'memory' backend.

server.address.description: Network address and port for the DHCP server to listen on (e.g., '192.168.1.1:67' or ':67' for all interfaces).

server.ipv6_enabled.description: Enable or disable IPv6 support (DHCPv6) in addition to IPv4 (DHCPv4).

server.log_level.description: Verbosity of server logging. Options: debug, info, warn, error.

block_size.description: Uniform block size in bytes for both IFILE and OFILE (conflicts with ibs/obs). For pt devices, must match device logical block size.

blocks_per_transfer.description: Number of input blocks per transfer buffer (BPT). Controls copy buffer size: IBS * BPT. Must satisfy ((IBS * BPT) % OBS == 0).

cdb_size.description: SCSI CDB size in bytes (0=auto, or 6,10,12,16,32). 0 uses auto-selection logic.

cmd_duration_limit.description: Command duration limit (CDL) value (0-7). 0 means no limit. Only effective with cdbsz >= 16.

continue_on_error.description: Continue copying despite input errors (coe=1). Not effective for output errors on regular files.

copy_blocks.description: Number of blocks to copy. -1 means 'all available'.

dry_run.description: Enable dry-run mode (--dry-run). Parses and validates arguments but skips actual I/O.

input_block_size.description: Input block size in bytes (conflicts with bs). Default: same as bs.

input_file.description: Input file/device path (required). Use '-' for stdin. Must be specified.

output_block_size.description: Output block size in bytes (conflicts with bs). Default: same as bs.

output_file.description: Output file/device path (optional). Defaults to /dev/null. Use '-' for stdout.

progress_report.description: Enable progress reporting (status=progress). Prints throughput/ETA periodically to stderr.

protect_read.description: RDPROTECT field for READ commands (0-7). Requires IFILE to be a pt device if >0.

protect_write.description: WRPROTECT field for WRITE commands (0-7). Requires OFILE to be a pt device if >0.

pt_access.description: Use SCSI pass-through (pt) access. Required for raw SCSI commands on devices that support both pt and standard I/O.

retries.description: Number of retries for transient SCSI errors on pt devices.

seek_blocks.description: Number of output blocks to seek before writing.

skip_blocks.description: Number of input blocks to skip before copying.

sparse_writes.description: Skip writing blocks that are entirely zero (sparse writes).

use_odx.description: Enable offloaded copy using ODX (XCOPY(LID4) subset).

use_xcopy.description: Enable offloaded copy using XCOPY(LID1) commands.

verbose_level.description: Verbose/diagnostic level (0-5). Higher values increase stderr output.

verify_mode.description: Enable verify mode (--verify). Compares IFILE and OFILE contents without copying.

cache_dns.description: Enable DNS caching to reduce lookups

foreground.description: Run in foreground (true) or as a background daemon (false)

host.description: The hostname or domain to update (e.g., example.dyndns.org or 'all.dnsomatic.com' for all registered IPs)

interface.description: Local IP address the web interface should bind to (e.g., 127.0.0.1 for localhost only)

interval.description: Update interval in seconds (only used in daemon mode)

log_file.description: Path to log file (set to empty string to disable file logging)

log_level.description: Minimum log level: debug, info, warning, error, or critical

password.description: Password or API token for the DNS service (required for most plugins)

plugin_option.description: Additional plugin-specific option string (e.g., 'hostname' for some plugins)

port.description: Port number for the internal web interface (use 0 to disable)

ssl_key.description: Path to TLS private key file

use_tls.description: Enable TLS/SSL for the web interface (requires valid cert/key)

user.description: Username for the DNS service (often email address or API username)

execute_command.description: Command to pass to the terminal application to load an external command within the terminal. Most terminal emulators support '-e' for this command.

terminal.description: Terminal application used for viewers that require a terminal.

artifacts_dir.description: Path to the directory where collected test artifacts (logs, reports, binaries) are stored.

compress_artifacts.description: Whether to compress artifacts (gzip) before saving them to disk to reduce storage usage.

health_endpoint.description: HTTP path for the health check endpoint (e.g., used by Kubernetes liveness/readiness probes).

listen_address.description: IP address the collector binds to. Use 0.0.0.0 for all interfaces, or a specific IP to restrict.

log_file.description: Path to the log file. Use '-' for standard error.

log_level.description: Verbosity of application logging.

max_artifact_size_mb.description: Maximum allowed size (in MiB) for a single artifact. Larger artifacts are rejected.

max_connections.description: Maximum number of simultaneous open connections allowed.

metrics_enabled.description: Whether to expose Prometheus-compatible metrics endpoint.

metrics_port.description: Port on which the metrics endpoint is served (if enabled).

port.description: TCP port on which the collector service accepts incoming HTTP requests.

workers.description: Number of worker processes to handle incoming requests. Set higher for high throughput.

config_filename.description: Path to the config database file.

passwords_filename.description: Path to the passwords database file.

templates_filename.description: Path to the templates database file.

force.description: Force non-interactive mode, answering 'No' to all questions (same as -f).

guess_depends.description: Comma-separated list of suffixes to treat as dependencies of the base package name.

info_cmd.description: Command used to display package information.

keep_sections.description: Comma-separated list of package sections to always keep.

keeper_file.description: Path to the file storing the list of kept/orphaned packages.

max_priority.description: Highest priority level to ask questions about. Possible values: required, important, standard, optional, extra, or ANY.

negative_keepers.description: Whether to respect negative entries (explicit removals) in the keeper file.

nokeep_sections.description: Comma-separated list of package sections to never keep.

quiet.description: Suppress all prompts (same as -q).

remove_cmd.description: Command used to remove packages (with purge).

use_essential.description: Consider packages marked 'Essential: yes' as keepers.

use_hold.description: Consider packages marked with 'hold' status as keepers.

use_tasks.description: Treat tasksel tasks as regular packages (prefixed 'task-').

verbose.description: Enable verbose output (same as -v on command line).

apt.use_debian_edu_repo.description: Include the official Debian-Edu APT repository (recommended for full feature set).

debian_edu.enabled.description: Enable or disable all Debian-Edu-specific customizations.

debian_edu.hostname_prefix.description: Prefix for automatically generated hostnames (e.g., 'edu', 'school'). Leave empty to disable.

enabled.description: Enable the content filter service.

log_level.description: Logging verbosity: 'debug', 'info', 'warn', or 'error'.

mode.description: Filtering mode: 'block' (default), 'monitor', or 'off'. In 'monitor' mode, violations are logged but not blocked.

admin_server.description: Hostname or IP address of the Kerberos admin server (for password changes, etc.).

enabled.description: Enable the Kerberos 5 connector plugin.

kdc.description: Hostname or IP address of the KDC server for the realm.

keytab.description: Path to keytab file for service principal authentication. Leave blank if not used.

krb5_conf.description: Path to the system Kerberos configuration file.

log_level.description: Logging verbosity level (debug, info, warning, error).

max_ttl.description: Maximum renewable ticket lifetime in seconds.

realm.description: Kerberos realm used for authentication (e.g., the institution's realm).

service_principal.description: Kerberos service principal (used with keytab if provided).

group_base.description: Optional custom base DN for group searches. Defaults to `ldap_base_dn` if empty.

ldap_base_dn.description: Base DN for LDAP searches (e.g., the root of your directory tree).

ldap_bind_dn.description: Distinguished Name (DN) used to bind to the LDAP directory for read-only access.

ldap_bind_password.description: Password for the bind DN. Keep secret; consider using a secure credential store in production.

ldap_ca_cert_path.description: Path to CA certificate file for verifying LDAP server identity (e.g., `/etc/ssl/certs/ldap-ca.crt`). Optional; leave empty to skip verification.

ldap_port.description: Port number for the LDAP server (typically 389 for non-SSL, 636 for LDAPS).

ldap_server.description: Hostname or IP address of the LDAP server to connect to.

ldap_use_ssl.description: Whether to use SSL/TLS for the LDAP connection (recommended for production).

sync_enabled.description: Enable automatic synchronization of users and groups from LDAP.

user_base.description: Optional custom base DN for user searches. Defaults to `ldap_base_dn` if empty.

enabled.description: Enable or disable the mDNS reflector service.

log_file.description: Path to a dedicated log file, or leave empty / set to 'syslog' to use the system logger.

log_level.description: Logging verbosity level. Choose from: debug, info, notice, warning, error, critical.

max_queries_per_second.description: Maximum number of mDNS queries per second to reflect. Helps prevent reflection storms.

max_reflected_entries.description: Maximum number of simultaneous mDNS entries (hosts, services) to track and reflect. Prevents memory exhaustion on large networks.

record_ttl.description: Time-to-live (in seconds) for reflected mDNS records. Controls how long reflected entries remain valid.

debug.description: Enable maximum debug output (–debug / -d).

gnupg_program.description: The name (or pathname) of the GnuPG program to use (DEBSIG_GNUPG_PROGRAM).

list_policies.description: List policies that passed Selection phase, without verification (–list-policies).

quiet.description: Suppress all output except fatal errors (–quiet / -q).

root_dir.description: Use a different root directory when looking up for policies and OpenPGP keyrings.

use_policy.description: Policy file name (without path) to use for verification. Overrides automatic selection.

verbose.description: Increase output verbosity to show execution steps (–verbose / -v).

AllowUnsafePermissions.description: If true, allow unsafe options (e.g., host /dev, /proc) in debspawn run.

BootstrapTool.description: Bootstrap tool (must be compatible with debootstrap interface).

CachePackages.description: If false, debspawn will not manage its own APT package cache.

DefaultBootstrapVariant.description: Default variant used for bootstrapping with debootstrap. Set to 'none' for no variant.

InjectedPkgsDir.description: Directory for pre-injected package files (root or per-image subdirs).

ResultsDir.description: Default output directory for build artifacts.

debug.description: Enable verbose debug logging (not recommended in production)

state_dir.description: Directory to store persistent state (jobs, workers, etc.)

tmp_dir.description: Directory for temporary files (e.g., uploaded artifacts)

signing_key_id.description: Human-readable identifier for the signing key. If empty, the key's fingerprint will be used automatically.

signing_key_passphrase.description: Passphrase to decrypt the private key (if encrypted). Leave empty for unencrypted keys.

signing_key_path.description: Absolute path to the private signing key file (e.g., RSA/EC private key in PEM format).

signing_signature_ttl.description: Time-to-live for generated signatures in seconds (e.g., 31536000 = 1 year). After this, signatures expire.

verify_max_signature_age.description: Maximum age (in seconds) for accepted signatures. Older signatures are rejected (e.g., 2592000 = 30 days).

verify_require_trusted_key.description: If true, verification fails if the signing key is not explicitly trusted. If false, falls back to allowing keys in the trusted keys path if no match is found.

verify_trusted_keys_path.description: Path to a directory containing trusted public keys (PEM format), or a file containing concatenated trusted keys.

hour_end.description: Ending hour of the hourly range

hour_start.description: Starting hour of the hourly range

path.description: PATH environment variable for cron jobs

shell.description: Shell used to execute cron commands

modules.default: battery ac processor button fan thermal video
modules.description: Space-separated list of kernel modules to load before starting acpid; use "all" to load all acpi drivers, or leave empty/commented to load none

options.description: Additional command-line options to pass to acpid (as a string to be appended to the acpid command)

defgroup.description: Group under which the ample service runs

defuser.description: User account under which the ample service runs

start_ample.description: Whether the ample service should start by default

ARGS.description: Global command-line arguments passed to arpwatch.

INTERFACES.description: Space-separated list of network interfaces to monitor.

PCAP_FILTER.description: pcap filter string to ignore specific packets.

RUNAS.description: Username to drop privileges and run as. Leave empty to run as root.

DISKCHECK.description: Disk usage percentage threshold to illuminate disk LED (0-100), or OFF

LOG.description: Directory where log files are stored

POWERON.description: Default power-on time in 24-hour HH:MM format

ROOT.description: Root partition for disk usage check

SHUTDOWN.description: Default shutdown time in 24-hour HH:MM format

WORK.description: Working partition for disk usage check

ionice_setting.description: IONICE setting for the BackupPC daemon (e.g., 'idle', 'best-effort:6'). Empty string disables IONICE.

nice_value.description: Nice value for the BackupPC daemon (e.g., 0, 10, 19). Higher means lower priority.

data_dir.description: Directory to persist jobs to disk (enables durability). Empty string disables persistence.

listen_host.description: IP address or hostname for the primary listen socket (e.g., '0.0.0.0' for all interfaces).

listen_port.description: Port number for the primary listen socket.

bluetooth_id.description: Bluetooth device address (MAC) to monitor; multiple devices may be space-separated

interval.description: Interval in milliseconds to check signal strength

arbitrator.description: IP addresses defining Raft arbitrators that help reach consensus.

arbitrator-group.description: System group for the boothd process on the arbitrator.

arbitrator-user.description: System user for the boothd process on the arbitrator.

attr-prereq.description: Expression to test site GEO attributes (format: <grant_type> <name> <op> <value>).

authfile.description: File containing the shared secret authentication key.

before-acquire-handler.description: Path to a script or directory containing pre-acquisition verification programs.

debug.description: Debug output level (alternative to command-line argument).

mode.description: Ticket control mode; automatic uses Raft algorithm, manual is admin-controlled.

renewal-freq.description: Ticket renewal frequency period in seconds.

site.description: IP addresses defining Raft member sites that can acquire tickets.

site-group.description: System group for the boothd process on cluster sites.

site-user.description: System user for the boothd process on cluster sites.

ticket.description: Ticket names to be registered and managed.

transport.description: Transport protocol for Raft exchanges. Currently only UDP is supported.

weights.description: Comma-separated integers defining Raft member weights; defaults to 0 for all.

DAEMON_OPTS.description: Additional command-line options passed to the brightd daemon

START_BRIGHTD.description: Whether brightd should be started on login (must be 'true' to enable)

BTRFS_ALLOW_CONCURRENCY.description: If true, allow concurrent btrfs maintenance jobs (otherwise they run in FIFO order).

BTRFS_BALANCE_DUSAGE.description: Usage percent range for balancing data block groups (space-separated min max).

BTRFS_BALANCE_MOUNTPOINTS.description: Colon-separated list of mountpoints/filesystems to balance periodically. 'auto' means all mounted btrfs filesystems.

BTRFS_BALANCE_MUSAGE.description: Usage percent for balancing metadata block groups (and mixed blockgroups).

BTRFS_BALANCE_PERIOD.description: Frequency of periodic balance. Valid values: none, daily, weekly, monthly. Also supports systemd.time(7) calendar events.

BTRFS_DEFRAG_MIN_SIZE.description: Minimal file size to consider for defragmentation.

BTRFS_DEFRAG_PATHS.description: Colon-separated list of paths to defragment periodically. Empty means none.

BTRFS_DEFRAG_PERIOD.description: Frequency of periodic defragmentation. Valid values: none, daily, weekly, monthly. Also supports systemd.time(7) calendar events.

BTRFS_LOG_OUTPUT.description: Output target for messages. Valid values: none, stdout, journal, syslog.

BTRFS_SCRUB_MOUNTPOINTS.description: Colon-separated list of mountpoints/filesystems to scrub periodically. 'auto' means all mounted btrfs filesystems.

BTRFS_SCRUB_PERIOD.description: Frequency of periodic scrub. Valid values: none, weekly, monthly. Also supports systemd.time(7) calendar events.

BTRFS_SCRUB_PRIORITY.description: I/O priority for scrub. Valid values: idle, normal.

BTRFS_SCRUB_READ_ONLY.description: If true, perform read-only scrub without attempting repairs.

BTRFS_TRIM_MOUNTPOINTS.description: Colon-separated list of mountpoints/filesystems to trim periodically. 'auto' means all mounted btrfs filesystems.

BTRFS_TRIM_PERIOD.description: Frequency of periodic trim. Valid values: none, daily, weekly, monthly. Also supports systemd.time(7) calendar events.

HIGHLIGHT_COLOUR.description: ANSI color code for highlighting (e.g., 31 = red)

net.host.description: Specifies the IP address or host name of the qnetd server.

net.keep_active_partition_tie_breaker.description: Specifies if keep active partition tie breaker should be used.

net.port.description: Specifies TCP port of qnetd server.

net.tie_breaker.description: Used as a fallback if qdevice has to decide between two or more equal partitions.

net.tls.description: Specifies if TLS should be used.

sync_timeout.description: Specifies how often corosync-qdevice should call the votequorum_qdevice_poll function during a sync phase.

timeout.description: Specifies how often corosync-qdevice should call the votequorum_qdevice_poll function.

votes.description: The number of votes provided to the cluster by qdevice.

COROSYNC_QNETD_RUNAS.description: User under which qnetd daemon should be running (empty means default user)

extra_opts.description: Extra options for cron daemon (e.g., '-L 5' for logging exit statuses).

read_env.description: Whether to read the system's default environment files (typically 'yes' or 'no').

chroot_path.description: Chroot directory for security hardening (empty = disabled).

forward_host.description: Hostname or IP of the upstream recursive resolver (e.g., Unbound or systemd-resolved).

forward_port.description: Port of the upstream recursive resolver (usually 53).

listen_ip.description: IP address on which curvedns listens for incoming DNS queries (UDP/TCP).

audio_gain.description: Audio output gain (0–100), only applicable if cwdaemon is built with audio support.

weight.description: Dit/dah timing weight (50 = straight key; lower = faster dits, higher = slower dits).

wpm.description: Morse code transmit speed in words per minute (WPM).

bind_address.description: IP address to bind to; becomes `-l <address>`.

db_dir.description: Directory for chroot and DB persistence; used in --chroot $DIR.

enable_compression.description: Enable compression. Not used directly in init script.

enable_dns_lookups.description: Enable reverse DNS lookups; becomes `-r` when true.

enable_graphing.description: Enable graphing. Not used directly in init script, but darkstat uses -g option if set.

graph_dir.description: Directory for daily graph data. Not used directly in init script, but darkstat uses -g option if set.

graph_retention_days.description: Retention days for graphs. Not used directly in init script.

max_hosts.description: Maximum hosts. Not used directly in init script; darkstat uses -m option if set.

max_ports.description: Maximum ports per host. Not used directly in init script.

port.description: TCP port for the web UI; becomes `-p <port>`.

start_enabled.description: Whether to set START_DARKSTAT=yes in /etc/darkstat/init.cfg (controls if darkstat starts on boot).

config_file_disable_https_check.description: If true, disables HTTPS certificate validation (mirrors --disable-https-check).

config_file_mailto.description: Email address to which reports are sent in --cron mode. May contain macros (%s(hostname|fqdn|ip)s).

config_file_report.description: Controls whether debsecan does any processing in --cron mode.

config_file_source.description: URL from which vulnerability information is fetched. If empty, the built-in default is used.

config_file_subject.description: Subject line of email reports. May contain macros (%s(hostname|fqdn|ip)s).

dhcp_helper_extra_opts.description: Complete command-line options string passed to dhcp-helper, combining servers, interfaces, and other flags.

drop_invalid_checksums.description: Whether to drop packets with invalid IP/UDP checksums (recommended for security and reliability).

log_level.description: Verbosity level for logging (debug, info, notice, warning, error, crit, alert, emerg).

max_packet.description: Maximum packet size in bytes to accept (RFC recommends 576 for relay, but many networks use larger).

port.description: UDP port on which to listen for incoming DHCP requests.

source_addr.description: Source IP address to use when relaying packets to servers. Leave empty to let the system choose.

syslog_facility.description: Syslog facility to use for logging (e.g., daemon, local0–local7).

enable_daemon.description: Whether to enable the didiwiki daemon (yes/no)

listen.description: IP address on which the didiwiki daemon will listen

daemon_args.description: Additional options passed to the diod daemon.

diod_enable.description: Whether to enable the diod server at startup.

--expand-hosts.description: Add domain to simple names in /etc/hosts.

--fast-dns-retry.description: DNS retry delay parameters in milliseconds.

minimum_uid.description: Minimum UID required for a user to be eligible for auto-login (prevents system accounts from auto-logging in).

pid_file.description: Path to the PID file used by nodm for process tracking.

user.description: Username to automatically log in. Must exist on the system.

xserver_options.description: Command-line arguments passed to the X server when starting (e.g., display number, virtual terminal, security options).

xsession.description: Command or script to execute as the user session (e.g., desktop environment launcher).

DAEMON_OPTS.description: Additional options that are passed to the Daemon.

separate_log.description: Enable separate logging to /var/log/nohang/nohang.log instead of system journal.

disable.description: Whether the service is disabled (inetd/xinetd style). Set to false to enable.

server_args_user.description: First argument passed to /usr/sbin/nullidentd. Typically matches the 'user' setting, but kept separate as per real config.

user.description: User account under which the daemon runs (for inetd/xinetd service definition).

-C.description: Treats inactive file cache as available memory.

-H.description: Transparent hugepage scan interval in milliseconds.

-K.description: Keeps interleaved memory distributed across NUMA nodes instead of merging.

-R.description: List of CPUs reserved for non-numad use.

-S.description: Scans all system processes instead of only explicitly included PIDs.

-m.description: Memory localization threshold percentage to stop moving process memory.

-p.description: Process PID to add to the explicit inclusion list for management.

-r.description: Process PID to remove from explicit inclusion/exclusion lists.

-t.description: Resource weight/value of logical CPUs as a percentage.

-w.description: Query parameter for recommended NUMA nodes (format: NCPUS[:MB]).

-x.description: Process PID to add to the explicit exclusion list.

oidentd_behind_proxy.description: Whether the host is behind a masquerading router acting as an oidentd proxy. Must be 'yes' or 'no'.

oidentd_limit_connections.description: Maximum number of simultaneous oidentd connections to allow.

oidentd_user.description: User account under which oidentd runs.

circuit_stream_timeout.description: Seconds until a stream is detached from a circuit and try a new circuit.

control_password.description: Tor control password or 'false' to use prompt/auto-generate.

descriptor_max_retries.description: Max retries when fetching a descriptor.

descriptor_timeout.description: Timeout in seconds when retrieving an Onion Service descriptor.

endpoints.description: The list of endpoints to be tested, including address, protocol, port, and paths.

get_certificate_info.description: Whether to get certificate information when testing TLS/HTTPS endpoints.

http_connect_max_retries.description: Max retries when doing a HTTP/HTTPS connection to an Onion Service.

interval.description: Max random time in seconds between probing each endpoint.

launch_tor.description: Whether to launch its own Tor daemon.

log_level.description: Sets the application log level.

metrics_port.description: Tor Metrics port. An empty value means it is disabled.

new_circuit.description: Whether to get a new circuit for every stream.

prometheus_exporter.description: Whether to enable Prometheus exporter functionality.

randomize.description: Whether to randomize the interval and sleep time for privacy.

rounds.description: Run only a limited number of rounds. Set to 0 to disable this limit.

shuffle.description: Whether to shuffle the endpoint list at each probing round.

sleep.description: Max random time in seconds to wait between each round of tests.

test_tls_connection.description: Whether to run a specific test for TLS endpoints.

tls_connect_max_retries.description: Max retries when doing a TLS connection to an Onion Service.

tor_address.description: Tor listening address if the system-wide service is used.

DefaultMemoryPressureDurationSec.description: Sets the amount of time a unit's control group needs to have exceeded memory pressure limits before systemd-oomd will take action.

DefaultMemoryPressureLimit.description: Sets the limit for memory pressure on the unit's control group before systemd-oomd will take action.

SwapUsedLimit.description: Sets the limit for memory and swap usage on the system before systemd-oomd will take action.

group.description: Group under which opendkim runs.

pid_file.description: Path to PID file. In legacy script uses $RUNDIR/$NAME.pid.

run_dir.description: Runtime directory for socket, PID file, and temp files (used in legacy script only).

socket.description: Socket address for communication with MTA (e.g., Postfix). Uses RUNDIR which defaults to /run/opendkim. Use 'local:path' for Unix domain sockets, 'inet:port@host' for TCP.

user.description: User under which opendkim runs.

group.description: System group for the OpenDMARC process.

run_dir.description: Runtime directory for PID file and Unix socket (e.g., /run/opendmarc or /var/spool/postfix/run/opendmarc).

user.description: System user account under which OpenDMARC runs (must have minimal privileges).

auto_restart.description: Automatically restart opensm if it crashes (useful for high-availability)

database_file.description: Path to persistent state database for SM failover/restart

database_persist.description: Persist SM state (LIDs, PKeys, GIDs) across restarts

default_priority.description: Priority assigned to backup SMs in a high-availability pair

gid_table.description: Enable GID table management (required for IPv6 over InfiniBand)

include_ports_only.description: If true, only ports listed in IncludedPort will be managed

log_file.description: Path to log file. Use '-' to log to stdout (for systemd journal)

log_level.description: Logging verbosity: 0=quiet, 1=minimal, 2=normal, 3=verbose, 4=debug

mad_timeout.description: Timeout (ms) for MAD responses before considering a request failed

max_mads.description: Maximum number of outstanding MAD requests (higher = more concurrent operations)

max_retries.description: Maximum number of restart attempts before giving up

num_threads.description: Number of threads to handle MADs — higher improves throughput on large fabrics

pkey_table.description: Enable PKey table management (required for partition key support)

ports.description: List of port GUIDs (in hex) or special value 'ALL'/'NONE' to control which ports opensm starts on

primary_port_guid.description: Port GUID to use for SM operations (0 = auto-select first IB port)

priority.description: SM priority (1–15). Lower values have higher priority in master election

qos.description: Enable QoS support (required if QoS policies are configured in fabric)

retry_delay.description: Seconds to wait before attempting a restart

sl2vl.description: Enable SL to VL mapping (required for SL-to-VL reassignment)

sm_mode.description: Mode of operation: 'master' (primary SM), 'backup' (standby), or 'standalone' (no peer)

split_mode.description: Enable split-mode for fabrics with physically separate subnets on dual-ported cards

p910nd_num.description: Printer number (empty string for default/only printer; non-empty string used for multi-printer setups).

p910nd_opts.description: Additional command-line arguments to pass directly to p910nd (e.g., '-f' to fork to background).

p910nd_start.description: Set to 1 to enable start by default on Debian (0 = disabled by default).

PCSCD_ARGS.description: Passes command-line arguments to the pcscd daemon.

PCSCLITE_FILTER_EXTEND_READER_NAMES.description: String to append to PC/SC reader names.

PCSCLITE_FILTER_IGNORE_READER_NAMES.description: Smart card reader names to ignore.

imap4_enabled.description: Set to "yes" to run IMAP4 service; any other value disables it.

imap4_flags.description: Additional command-line flags passed to perdition when running in IMAP4 mode.

imaps_enabled.description: Set to "yes" to run IMAP4S (IMAP over SSL/TLS) service; any other value disables it.

imaps_flags.description: Additional command-line flags passed to perdition when running in IMAP4S mode.

managesieve_enabled.description: Set to "yes" to run ManageSieve service; any other value disables it.

managesieve_flags.description: Additional command-line flags passed to perdition when running in ManageSieve mode.

pop3_enabled.description: Set to "yes" to run POP3 service; any other value disables it.

pop3_flags.description: Additional command-line flags passed to perdition when running in POP3 mode.

pop3s_enabled.description: Set to "yes" to run POP3S (POP3 over SSL/TLS) service; any other value disables it.

pop3s_flags.description: Additional command-line flags passed to perdition when running in POP3S mode.

run_perdition.description: Set to "yes" to run perdition; any other value disables it (overrides all other settings).

extra_opts.description: Additional command-line options passed to the Perlbal daemon. Empty by default.

group.description: Group under which Perlbal runs. Optional; comment out to omit.

perlbal_enable.description: If true, Perlbal will be started via the init system.

user.description: User account under which Perlbal runs.

bytes.description: Size in bytes to transmit and receive each time for entropy exchange.

cache_enabled.description: Enable caching of entropy responses (e.g., for low-entropy sources).

cache_max_entries.description: Maximum number of entries in the entropy cache.

device_path.description: Filesystem path to the entropy source device (e.g., /dev/random or /dev/urandom).

health_endpoint_path.description: HTTP path for the health check endpoint.

http_port.description: HTTP port on which the pollen server should listen and respond (unencrypted).

https_port.description: HTTPS port on which the pollen server should listen and respond (TLS-encrypted).

listen_addr.description: IP address the web server will bind to.

log_level.description: Verbosity of server logs.

max_concurrent_requests.description: Maximum number of simultaneous incoming requests the server will handle.

metrics_endpoint_path.description: HTTP path for the Prometheus-style metrics endpoint.

rate_limit_rps.description: Maximum requests per second per client (when rate limiting enabled).

timeout_connect.description: Timeout (seconds) for connecting to the entropy source.

timeout_read.description: Timeout (seconds) for reading entropy from the source.

timeout_write.description: Timeout (seconds) for writing response to client.

tls_cert_file.description: Path to the TLS certificate file.

tls_key_file.description: Path to the TLS private key file.

worker_count.description: Number of worker processes to spawn.

BINARY.description: Convert hex text output into binary data instead of sha512sum format.

CURL_OPTS.description: Options to pass through to curl(1).

DEVICE.description: Device to seed the PRNG with.

POOL.description: Remote pollen(8) server pool to interact with.

SERVER.description: Remote pollen(8) server to interact with.

WAIT.description: Time in seconds to wait for a response from the server.

CONF.description: Path to the main postfwd ruleset configuration file.

INET.description: IP address where postfwd listens for incoming connections.

STARTUP.description: Set to 1 to enable startup in daemon mode.

history_dir.description: Directory where preload stores access history (patterns of file reads) for learning.

max_processes.description: Maximum number of processes the daemon will track simultaneously. Larger values increase memory usage.

passive.description: Whether to reactively read ahead *only* when a process actually opens a file.

preload_iosched.description: I/O scheduling class to use for preload (e.g., '--iosched idle').

proactive.description: Whether to proactively load files for frequently-used processes *before* they are opened (improves responsiveness, but may increase disk usage).

profile_dir.description: Directory where preload stores readahead profiles for known files and applications.

readahead_pages.description: Maximum number of pages to read ahead per I/O request. Set to 0 to use the kernel's default value.

scan_interval.description: How often (in seconds) the daemon scans the system for new processes and updates its database.

action.description: Specifies the command to run by the system shell when the trigger condition evaluates to true.

occurs.description: Specifies how many times an action should be performed on matching processes.

perl-action.description: Specifies Perl statements to be evaluated, useful for initialization, cleanup, or cross-process logic.

trigger.description: Specifies the condition on which a process action is fired, evaluated as a Perl expression.

ALERT_ALL.description: Send email for all new bad packets instead of only when danger level increases.

AUTO_IDS_DANGER_LEVEL.description: Danger level a scan must reach before psad automatically blocks the IP.

DANGER_LEVEL1.description: Number of dropped packets required to assign danger level 1.

DANGER_LEVEL2.description: Number of dropped packets required to assign danger level 2.

DANGER_LEVEL3.description: Number of dropped packets required to assign danger level 3.

DANGER_LEVEL4.description: Number of dropped packets required to assign danger level 4.

DANGER_LEVEL5.description: Number of dropped packets required to assign danger level 5.

EMAIL_ADDRESSES.description: Comma-separated list of email addresses to which email alerts will be sent.

EMAIL_ALERT_DANGER_LEVEL.description: Danger level a scan must reach before any email alert is sent.

ENABLE_AUTO_IDS.description: Dynamically block traffic from IPs reaching a configurable danger level via iptables/tcpwrappers.

ENABLE_DSHIELD_ALERTS.description: Send parsed iptables log messages to dshield.org.

ENABLE_PERSISTENCE.description: Keep all scans in memory without timeout to discover stealthy scans.

FW_MSG_SEARCH.description: Set of search strings to identify iptables messages to parse when FW_SEARCH_ALL is N.

FW_SEARCH_ALL.description: Search mode for parsing iptables messages. Y parses all, N restricts to search strings.

HOME_NET.description: Internal network(s) connected to the local system in CIDR notation, comma-separated.

HOSTNAME.description: Hostname of the machine on which psad is running, used in email alerts.

IGNORE_CONNTRACK_BUG_PKTS.description: Ignore TCP packets with ACK or RST flags to avoid false positives from conntrack bugs.

IGNORE_PORTS.description: Comma-separated list of port ranges and/or individual ports and corresponding protocols to completely ignore.

IMPORT_OLD_SCANS.description: Preserve scan data across restarts or reboots by importing filesystem cache data.

PORT_RANGE_SCAN_THRESHOLD.description: Minimum difference between lowest and highest scanned port before alerting.

PSAD_EMAIL_LIMIT.description: Maximum emails sent per scanning IP to prevent alert flooding.

SCAN_TIMEOUT.description: Seconds to remove packets from scan threshold calculation when persistence is off.

SHOW_ALL_SIGNATURES.description: Display all detected signatures from a single IP since scan start, not just newly detected.

SNORT_SID_STR.description: String kmsgsd searches for in iptables log messages generated by fwsnort.

enforce_src.description: If true, only accept ICMP packets from IPs listed in allowed_src_nets.

listen_interface.description: Network interface to listen on. Use 'auto' to let ptunnel auto-detect.

log_file.description: Path to log file. Leave empty to log only to stdout/stderr.

max_idle_time.description: Maximum inactivity (in seconds) before a tunnel is forcibly closed.

max_tunnels.description: Maximum number of concurrent tunnels (TCP connections) allowed.

password.description: Password for securing the tunnel. Must be identical on both client and server.

ping_delay.description: Delay (in milliseconds) between consecutive ping packets. Lower = more aggressive, higher = more reliable through firewalls.

ping_dest_port.description: ICMP destination port used in the ICMP tunnel (must match between client and server). 0 = echo request.

ping_size.description: Size (in bytes) of ICMP payload. Larger sizes may improve throughput but increase fragmentation.

ping_ttl.description: Time-to-live (TTL) value for outgoing ICMP packets. 0 = use system default.

remote_dst.description: Target remote IP address for the ICMP tunnel (required on the receiving end).

run_daemon.description: Set to "true" to enable the ptunnel daemon (must be set to 'true' to start the service).

tunnel_timeout.description: Timeout (in seconds) after which an idle tunnel is closed.

verbose.description: Enable verbose logging? If true, logs at normal level. Use 0 or 1 explicitly for fine control.

password.description: Sets the password for challenge-response authentication; must match the client.

run_daemon.description: Controls whether ptunnel runs in the background as a daemon.

--ipc-namespace.description: Enable a new IPC namespace for regular users.

--iprange.description: Assign an IP address from a specified range to the interface.

--join.description: Join an existing sandbox by name or PID.

--join-filesystem.description: Join the mount namespace of an existing sandbox (root only).

--join-network.description: Join the network namespace of an existing sandbox (root only).

--join-or-start.description: Join an existing sandbox or start a new one with the specified name.

--keep-config-pulse.description: Disable automatic PulseAudio config initialization in private home.

--keep-dev-ntsync.description: Allow access to /dev/ntsync even with private-dev enabled.

--keep-dev-shm.description: Keep /dev/shm untouched when private-dev is enabled.

--keep-fd.description: Inherit specific file descriptors or all open descriptors into the sandbox.

--keep-shell-rc.description: Disable copying system templates to private home to preserve original shell configs.

--landlock.enforce.description: Enforce experimental Landlock file access rules.

--landlock.fs.execute.description: Add a Landlock execution permission rule for a path.

--landlock.fs.makedev.description: Allow creation of block/character devices beneath a path via Landlock.

--landlock.fs.makeipc.description: Allow creation of FIFOs and Unix sockets beneath a path via Landlock.

--landlock.fs.read.description: Add a Landlock read access rule for a path.

--landlock.fs.write.description: Add a Landlock write access rule for a path.

--ls.description: List files inside a sandbox container.

--mac.description: Assign a MAC address to the sandbox's network interface.

--machine-id.description: Spoof /etc/machine-id with a random ID inside the sandbox.

--memory-deny-write-execute.description: Block writable and executable memory mappings via seccomp.

--mkdir.description: Create a directory inside the user's home.

--mkfile.description: Create an empty file inside the user's home.

--mtu.description: Set the MTU value for the sandbox network interface.

--name.description: Set a custom name for the sandbox to reference in other commands.

--net.description: Enable a network namespace connected to a bridge, physical interface, tap device, or isolate it completely.

--net.print.description: Print network interface configuration for a sandbox.

--netfilter.description: Enable a default firewall or load a custom iptables filter file.

--netfilter.print.description: Print the firewall rules installed in a sandbox.

--netfilter6.description: Enable an IPv6 firewall specified by filename.

--netfilter6.print.description: Print the IPv6 firewall rules in a sandbox.

--netlock.description: Monitor network traffic during startup and lock the firewall to only allowed IPs.

--netmask.description: Set the subnet mask for a manually configured IP address.

--netns.description: Run the program in a pre-existing named network namespace.

--netstats.description: Monitor network traffic statistics for all sandboxes.

--nettrace.description: Monitor TCP, UDP, and ICMP traffic for a sandbox or system namespace.

--nice.description: Set the process priority (nice value) for sandboxed processes.

--no3d.description: Disable 3D hardware acceleration inside the sandbox.

--noblacklist.description: Disable blacklisting for specific files or directories.

--nodvd.description: Disable DVD and audio CD device access.

--noexec.description: Remount files or directories with noexec, nodev, and nosuid flags.

--nogroups.description: Disable supplementary group memberships for the sandbox.

--nonewprivs.description: Set NO_NEW_PRIVS to prevent privilege escalation via setuid binaries.

--noprofile.description: Do not load any security profile.

--noroot.description: Create a user namespace where root does not exist.

--notpm.description: Disable Trusted Platform Module (TPM) device access.

--notv.description: Disable DVB (Digital Video Broadcasting) TV device access.

--nowhitelist.description: Disable whitelisting for specific files or directories.

--oom.description: Set the Out-Of-Memory killer score for the sandbox.

--output.description: Log stdout to a file with automatic rotation (max 500KB per file).

--output-stderr.description: Log both stdout and stderr to a file with rotation.

--private.description: Mount a temporary filesystem for /home and /root.

--private-bin.description: Build a temporary /bin containing only specified executables.

--private-cache.description: Mount an empty temporary filesystem over ~/.cache.

--private-cwd.description: Set the sandbox working directory to home or a custom path.

--private-dev.description: Create a new /dev with only essential device nodes.

--private-etc.description: Copy specified /etc files/groups into a temporary filesystem.

--private-home.description: Build a temporary user home containing only specified files/directories.

--private-opt.description: Build a temporary /opt containing specified files/directories.

--private-srv.description: Build a temporary /srv containing specified files/directories.

--private-tmp.description: Mount an empty temporary filesystem over /tmp while preserving X11/Pulse sockets.

--profile.description: Load a custom security profile by filename or profile name.

--profile.print.description: Print the profile filename used for a sandbox.

--protocol.description: Enable seccomp-based filtering for specific socket protocols.

--protocol.print.description: Print the protocol filter active in a sandbox.

--put.description: Upload a file into a sandbox container.

--read-only.description: Mount files or directories as read-only inside the sandbox.

--read-write.description: Mount files or directories as read-write inside the sandbox.

--restrict-namespaces.description: Block creation of new namespaces via seccomp.

--rlimit-as.description: Set maximum virtual memory size (address space) in bytes.

--rlimit-cpu.description: Set maximum CPU time in seconds before killing sandboxed processes.

--rlimit-fsize.description: Set maximum file size a process can create.

--rlimit-nofile.description: Set maximum number of open files per process.

--rlimit-nproc.description: Set maximum number of processes per real user ID.

--rlimit-sigpending.description: Set maximum number of pending signals for a process.

--rmenv.description: Remove a specific environment variable from the sandbox.

--scan.description: ARP-scan networks from inside a network namespace to detect macvlan drivers.

--seccomp.description: Enable seccomp filtering with default or custom syscall groups/lists.

blink.description: Whether to blink the applet icon on status change

blink_count.description: Number of times to blink the icon on status change

notifications.description: Whether to show notifications when firewall status changes

shields_down.description: Action to take when firewall is inactive (e.g., public, private)

shields_up.description: Action to take when firewall is active (e.g., block, allow)

show_inactive.description: Whether to show inactive firewall connections in the applet

CleanupModulesOnExit.description: If set to yes or true the firewall related kernel modules will be unloaded on exit or stop of firewalld.

DefaultZone.description: The default zone used if an empty zone string is used.

FlushAllOnReload.description: Flush all runtime rules on a reload.

IPv6_rpfilter.description: Performs reverse path filtering (RPF) on IPv6 packets as per RFC 3704.

IndividualCalls.description: Do not use combined -restore calls, but individual calls. This increases the time needed but is useful for debugging.

LogDenied.description: Add logging rules right before reject and drop rules in the INPUT, FORWARD and OUTPUT chains.

NftablesCounters.description: If set to yes, add a counter to every nftables rule. This is useful for debugging and comes with a small performance cost.

NftablesFlowtable.description: This may improve forwarded traffic throughput by enabling nftables flowtable. The value is a space separated list of interfaces.

NftablesTableOwner.description: If set to yes, the generated nftables rule set will be owned exclusively by firewalld to prevent accidental or malicious modification.

RFC3964_IPv4.description: As per RFC 3964, filter IPv6 traffic with 6to4 destination addresses that correspond to IPv4 addresses that should not be routed over the public internet.

ReloadPolicy.description: Policy during reload. By default all traffic except for established connections is dropped while the rules are updated.

StrictForwardPorts.description: If set to yes, the generated destination NAT (DNAT) rules will NOT accept traffic that was DNAT'd by other entities.

action_timeout.description: Seconds before action buttons disappear (0 = never expire)

autostart.description: Whether to automatically start fnott at user login

config_dir.description: Base directory for fnott runtime files (e.g., state, pid, icons cache)

default_urgency.description: Default urgency level for new notifications: low, normal, critical

font.description: Font name and size for notification text (e.g., 'DejaVu Sans 9')

identity.description: FQDN (or URI) uniquely identifying this Diameter node.

log_file.description: Path to log file (or leave empty to log to stdout/syslog).

debug_level.description: Log verbosity: 0 (quiet), 1 (info), 2 (debug).

group.description: System group under which the agent processes run.

log_level.description: Verbosity level: 0=error, 1=warning, 2=info, 3=debug.
